feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: Pope Leo says he will gradually resume duties after cancer surgery
entry.summary: Pope Leo XIV thanked thousands of faithful in St. Peter's Square on Sunday for their prayers while he was hospitalized, and said he plans to gradually return to his usual duties.

entry.title: Carney says 4 service members killed and dozens injured in fire at Alberta military base
entry.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney described the incident as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military on domestic soil.

entry.title: Student protests widen into greater social unrest in France
entry.summary: Hundreds of protests took place in cities across France. Most of them were peaceful but some turned chaotic and violent.

entry.title: The state of the State Department in the wake of the Kimberly Guilfoyle scandal
entry.summary: NPR's Joel Rose talks with James B. Story, former U.S. Ambassador to Venezuela, about the state of the State Department in the wake of the Kimberly Guilfoyle scandal.

entry.title: French police arrest 1,800 after violent clashes and looting mar protests
entry.summary: Police arrested at least 1,800 people across France after violent groups clashed with officers and looted shops during nationwide demonstrations that drew hundreds of thousands of people.

entry.title: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital days after lung cancer surgery
entry.summary: The Pope left Rome's Gemelli Hospital Saturday, days after surgery for lung cancer removed the lower lobe of his right lung. He is currently scheduled to travel to Latin America in November.

entry.title: Zelenskyy urges support for new US sanctions on Russia after Trump puts them on hold
entry.summary: Zelenskyy described the move as unfortunate, adding it would encourage Russia to continue its assault. Trump told Congress that the pause was in the national interest but gave no further details.

entry.title: Decades after apartheid, South Africans seek justice for crimes of the past
entry.summary:
More than three decades after the end of apartheid, families of victims of some of the worst crimes of South Africa's past
are still fighting for justice. As survivors and perpetrators grow older, a new wave of legal efforts is seeking truth, accountability and reparations before it's too late.

entry.title: Sidewalk sleepers: They have nowhere else to stay while a loved one is in the hospital
entry.summary: Patients travel miles to be treated at public hospitals in Delhi. Those in need get financial aid for their care. But for overnight accommodations, families are often on their own — and on the street.

entry.title: Israeli settlers beat Palestinians and a U.S. photojournalist in West Bank attacks
entry.summary: Masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians as they were harvesting olives in the occupied West Bank on Friday, injuring several people including a photojournalist working for The Washington Post.
